records.label: Tyk2-deficient patient

phenotypes.text: defective type I IFN, IL-6, IL-10, IL-12 and IL-23 signaling

quotes: Here we identified a homozygous Tyk2 mutation in a patient who had been clinically diagnosed with hyper-IgE syndrome.
This patient showed unusual susceptibility to various microorganisms including virus, fungi, and mycobacteria and suffered from atopic dermatitis with elevated serum IgE.

quotes: He was born in 1992 and was the third child of healthy, first-cousin parents. The patient was vaccinated with BCG at two months. At eight months, left axillary lymphadenopathy was detected
The patient is homozygous for a 9bp deletion in exon 16 of TYK2, c.2302_2310del or 2302del9, which creates a premature termination codon at position 767.
Serum IgE concentration were determined at the ages of 2, 11, 16 and 18 years, and were found to be normal or slightly high [80, 115, 218, 155 IU/ml, respectively]

records.label: P1
quotes: We investigated the previously reported Japanese TYK2-deficient patient (P1; Minegishi et al., 2006). He carries a homozygous 4-bp deletion in exon 4 (Fig. 1, A–C).

The first patient investigated was a Japanese man (P1) with consanguineous parents. As described elsewhere (Minegishi et al., 2006), P1 has displayed atopic dermatitis since the age of 1 mo and recurrent bacterial and viral infections since the age of 1 yr.
Immunological explorations have repeatedly revealed hypereosinophilia (701–800/µl) and high serum IgE concentrations (1,430–2,100 IU/ml).

records.label: P2
records.segregation: clinical disease observed in all homozygotes and only in homozygotes
quotes: There is a 9-bp deletion in exon 16, c.2303_2311del, in P2 from kindred B (Fig. 1, A–C; Grant et al., 2011).

The second patient is a Turkish man (P2) born to consanguineous parents (first-degree cousins). A detailed clinical study relating to this patient has recently been published elsewhere (Kilic et al., 2012).

this patient displayed disseminated BCG lymphadenitis at 21 mo of age and severe bacterial meningitis (with CFS cultures positive for Brucella spp.) at 8 yr of age, and at the age of 11 yr, he was diagnosed with shingles

records.label: P3
records.segregation: clinical disease observed in all homozygotes and only in homozygotes
quotes: In P3 and P4, from kindred C, there is a frameshift insertion of 1 bp in exon 23, c.3318_3319insC (Fig. 1, A–C).

P3 was hospitalized at the age of 13 yr with suspected abdominal tuberculosis. Despite antimycobacterial treatment, the abdominal complaints persisted, and P3 also suffered from ascitis and a psoas abscess that developed after a few months.
Treatment was restarted, but the patient was readmitted to hospital with bacterial meningitis and subsequently died, 15 mo after the initial onset of symptoms.

records.label: P4
records.segregation: clinical disease observed in all homozygotes and only in homozygotes
quotes: P3’s younger brother (P4) was hospitalized at the age of 8 mo for meningitis of unknown etiology. He suffered from recurrent otitis and urinary tract infections and presented asthma and eczema of the ear canal. His eosinophil levels were found to be high.
P4 is now 15 yr old, has no treatment, and is followed in Morocco.

records.label: P5

phenotypes.text: paravertebral and psoas abscesses with fistulization

records.segregation: clinical disease observed in all homozygotes and only in homozygotes
quotes: A nucleotide substitution in exon 5 (c.462G>T) in P5 and P6, from kindred D, leads to the creation of a premature stop codon at amino acid position 154 (E154X).

The fifth patient, P5, is a 5-yr-old boy born to consanguineous Iranian parents. He was vaccinated at birth with live BCG. At 2 and 4 mo of age, he developed right axillary lymphadenitis and multiple cervical lymphadenitis, respectively.
At the age of 4.5 yr, he developed paravertebral and psoas abscesses with fistulization and pulmonary involvement.

records.label: P6
records.segregation: clinical disease observed in all homozygotes and only in homozygotes
quotes: His younger sister (P6) is 2 yr old and was vaccinated with BCG at birth. She developed BCG lymphadenopathy, lasting for 1 mo, after vaccination. At the age of 1 yr, she was hospitalized for 1 wk for an unknown viral infection of the skin.

records.label: P7
records.segregation: clinical disease observed in all homozygotes and only in homozygotes
quotes: A frameshift deletion of 1 bp at position 149 in exon 3 in P7 (c.149delC), from kindred E, leads to the creation of a premature stop codon at position 50 in the protein (S50HfsX1).
The seventh patient is a 9-yr-old girl from Iran born to consanguineous parents.
spiral lung CT with contrast showed diffuse bilateral micronodular infiltrations associated with hilar and mediastinal adenopathies and cavitary consolidation in the right upper lobe.

records.label: P8
quotes: A nucleotide substitution (c.1912 C>T) at position 1912 in exon 13 in P8, from kindred F, creates a premature stop codon at position 638 (R638X; Fig. 1, A–C).

He successively suffered from herpes gingivostomatitis at 18 mo of age, aseptic meningitis (fever, vomiting, irritability, and altered mental state/reduced consciousness), and disseminated cutaneous herpetic lesions at 24 mo of age.
He also has mild mental disability, and it has not been clearly established whether this disability is congenital or occurred after meningitis.

quotes: We investigated a TYK2 deficient patient, presenting with eczema, skin abscesses, respiratory infections and IgE levels >1000 U/mL, without viral or mycobacterial infections
NK-cell phenotype and function, including IL-12/IL-18 mediated responses, were normal in the patient

records.label: P12 (Chinese boy)

phenotypes.text: BCG vaccination site abscess and ulceration

phenotypes.hpo_label: Reduced total natural killer cell count

quotes: The patient was a boy at the age of 1 year and 11 months, the second child in the family (parents are young and nonconsanguineous), who was born in 2016 and vaccinated with BCG vaccine on the third day after birth.
Sequence analysis demonstrated the homozygous missense mutation in the exon 17 of the TYK2 gene of the patient, which was heterozygous in his parents (Figure 1).

No high serum IgE concentration, atopy, staphylococcal illness, or lymphopenia was found for him. He started to say some simple words at the age of 3 years and 4 months with normal motor development. Physical examination revealed a small head circumference.

records.label: Five TYK2-deficient patients

phenotypes.text: recurrent infections with distinct pathogen profiles
impaired cytokine responses (IFN-alpha/beta/gamma, IL-6, IL-10, IL-12, IL-23)

quotes: We described five more TYK2-deficient cases presenting with or without hyper-IgE levels, atopy, and distinct pathogen infection profile, which are caused by novel TYK2 mutations.
The patients showed heterogeneous responses to various cytokine treatments, including IFN-α/β/γ, IL-6, IL-10, IL-12, and IL-23. The homeostasis of lymphocytes is also disrupted.

P2 was hospitalized for moderate COVID-19 pneumonia but did not require oxygen therapy.

quotes: The third was the 3-yr-old younger sister of P3, who carries the same genotype. She had a history of critical influenza pneumonia that required intubation and ventilation, as well as disseminated varicella. However, she was not infected with SARS-CoV-2 and she has remained seronegative to date (Fig. 1 C).

records.label: P4

phenotypes.text: critical COVID-19 pneumonia requiring ICU and high-flow oxygen

records.segregation: AR inheritance confirmed by family segregation analysis
quotes: P4 | TYK2 | AR | P216fs/P216fs (LOF) | M | 9 | Middle East/Turkey | Critical | | No adverse reaction to MMR vaccination | Recurrent bronchitis requiring hospital admission and inhaler therapy | Survived | This report
three unrelated patients had the same homozygous missense variant of TYK2 (P216fs*14; AR inheritance was confirmed for all three patients by family segregation analysis)

notes.statement: In an international cohort of 112 children hospitalized for COVID-19 pneumonia, Zhang et al. (2022) identified 3 unrelated Turkish children born to consanguineous parents who were homozygous for the same TYK2 frameshift variant (P216Rfs*14), previously shown to be loss-of-expression; the authors confirmed it was loss of function. They implicated AR TYK2 deficiency as a new genetic etiology of COVID-19 pneumonia.
quotes: Three of the five patients not previously reported, P2, P3, and P4, carried the same TYK2 variant (P216Rfs*14), which had already been shown experimentally to be loss-of-expression in cells from patients (Fuchs et al., 2016). We confirmed that this variant was LOF (not depicted).
Our findings implicate AR STAT2 and TYK2 deficiencies as new genetic etiologies of COVID-19 pneumonia.

notes.statement: Zhang et al. (2022) found that ACE2-transduced SV40 fibroblasts from a patient homozygous for TYK2 P216fs*14 did not control SARS-CoV-2 replication normally, were not protected by IFN-alpha-2b pretreatment, and failed to induce ISGs in response to infection or IFN-alpha-2b.
quotes: we found that cells from STAT2- and TYK2-deficient patients did not control viral replication normally (Fig. 4 A). Moreover, pretreatment of the cells with IFN-α2b blocked viral infection in healthy donor cells but not in patient cells (Fig. 4 A).
We found that cells from STAT2- and TYK2-deficient patients failed to induce ISG production in response to SARS-CoV-2 infection or IFN-α2b pretreatment (Fig. 4 B).

notes.statement: Zhang et al. (2022) considered the occurrence of critical COVID-19 pneumonia in unrelated TYK2-deficient patients surprising, because TYK2 deficiency impairs but does not abolish cellular responses to type I IFNs, and noted that more infected TYK2-deficient patients were needed to estimate penetrance, which may be incomplete.
quotes: The occurrence of critical pneumonia in three unrelated patients with TYK2 deficiency is more surprising. Indeed, TYK2 deficiency impairs, but does not abolish, cellular responses to type I IFNs (Boisson-Dupuis et al., 2018). More TYK2-deficient patients infected with SARS-CoV-2 need to be diagnosed to estimate the corresponding penetrance.

notes.statement: Lv et al. (2022) confirmed the pathogenic effects of novel TYK2 mutations by qRT-PCR, Western blot, and protein stability assays, and found heterogeneous responses of patient PBMCs to IFN-alpha/beta/gamma, IL-6, IL-10, IL-12, and IL-23. They proposed that TYK2 acts as a multi-tasker orchestrating various cytokine signaling pathways, with differentially combined defects accounting for the clinical manifestations.
quotes: Pathogenic effects of patients were confirmed by qRT-PCR, Western blot, and protein stability assays.
we propose that TYK2 works as a multi-tasker in orchestrating various cytokine signaling pathways, differentially combined defects which account for the expressed clinical manifestations.

notes.statement: Lv et al. (2022) noted that TYK2-deficient patients do not necessarily present with hyper-IgE syndrome features, with their patients presenting with or without elevated IgE and atopy.
quotes: accumulating evidence suggests TYK2-deficient patients do not necessarily present with HIES characteristics

notes.statement: Wu et al. (2020) found that the TYK2 G799R mutation decreased TYK2 mRNA expression in patient-derived cells, with no TYK2 protein detected by Western blot; in transfected HEK293T cells the mutant also decreased mRNA and protein expression of FLAG- and GFP-tagged TYK2.
quotes: The results showed that this mutation leads to a decrease of TYK2 mRNA expression (Figure 2A). Besides, the western blot results showed that no TYK2 protein expression found in the patient (Figure 2B).
The qRT-PCR results showed that this c.2395G>A mutant decreased the expression of FLAG-TYK2 and TYK2-GFP (Figure 3B).

notes.statement: Wu et al. (2020) noted that the c.2395G>A (G799R) variant was present in the gnomAD database, suggesting that it was not a private mutation.
quotes: this mutation type was is included in the genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD), suggesting that this was not a private mutation.

notes.statement: In a literature review of 12 patients with TYK2 deficiency, Wu et al. (2020) found that 58% had intracellular bacterial infections, 58% had recurrent viral infections, 25% had markedly increased serum IgE, and none had the facial, skeletal, dental, or vascular features of STAT3-related hyper-IgE syndrome.
quotes: Including our patient, there are 12 patients reported with TYK2 deficiency (Table 3), with the average age at diagnosis of 10.8 years old. Seven patients (58%) suffered from intracellular bacterial infections.
none of the 12 patients had special facial features, abnormal bone development or pathological fractures, delayed deciduous tooth loss, or aneurysms.

notes.statement: Fuchs et al. (2016) found that a TYK2 mutation completely abolished the IFN-alpha-mediated antiviral response in a monocyte assay. It partly reduced IL-10 signaling, which went with reduced IL-10R-beta expression, but did not reduce IL-6 signaling.
quotes: We established a novel simple diagnostic monocyte assay to show that the mutation completely abolishes the IFN-α mediated antiviral response. It also partly reduces IL-10 but not IL-6 mediated signaling associated with reduced IL-10Rβ expression.

notes.statement: Fuchs et al. (2016) found almost normal type III IFN signaling and only minimal impairment of virus control in a TYK2-deficient human cell line. They suggested that preserved type III IFN responses and normal NK-cell function may contribute to antiviral protection in TYK2 deficiency, leading to a surprisingly mild human phenotype.
quotes: we found almost normal type-III IFN signaling associated with minimal impairment of virus control in a TYK2 deficient human cell line
Thus, preserved type-III IFN responses and normal NK-cell function may contribute to antiviral protection in TYK2 deficiency leading to a surprisingly mild human phenotype.

notes.statement: Fuchs et al. (2016) established a simple diagnostic monocyte assay that detects loss of the IFN-alpha-mediated antiviral response in TYK2 deficiency.
quotes: We established a novel simple diagnostic monocyte assay to show that the mutation completely abolishes the IFN-α mediated antiviral response.

notes.statement: Kreins et al. (2015) found that none of the 7 newly identified TYK2-deficient patients had features of hyper-IgE syndrome (atopy, high serum IgE, or staphylococcal disease), and none had fungal infections or mucocutaneous candidiasis. They concluded that the core clinical phenotype of TYK2 deficiency is mycobacterial and/or viral infections.
quotes: Surprisingly, unlike P1, none of these seven newly identified TYK2-deficient patients displayed any of the features of HIES. In particular, they did not display atopy, high serum IgE concentration, or staphylococcal disease.
The core clinical phenotype of TYK2 deficiency is mycobacterial and/or viral infections, caused by impaired responses to IL-12 and IFN-α/β.

notes.statement: Kreins et al. (2015) identified 5 different homozygous null mutations in TYK2 in 7 patients from 5 kindreds originating from Turkey, Morocco, Iran, and Argentina. All 5 mutations were predicted to cause premature stop codons and were absent from public databases. TYK2 protein was undetectable in the patients' cells.
quotes: These five novel TYK2 mutations, like that of P1, are predicted to result in a premature stop codon. They are also private, as they are absent from our in-house WES database and all public databases (including NCBI, Ensembl, 1,000 genomes, and ExAc).
The 130-kD TYK2 protein, which was detectable in control cells, was undetectable in cells from all patients (Fig. 1, D and E; and see Fig. 4 A).

notes.statement: Kreins et al. (2015) found no individuals homozygous for TYK2 stop mutations in any database and only 84 heterozygous individuals.
quotes: There are no homozygous individuals for stop mutations in any database and only 84 heterozygous individuals.

notes.statement: Kreins et al. (2015) found that cells from all 8 TYK2-deficient patients had impaired but not abolished responses to IL-12, IL-23, IFN-alpha/beta, and IL-10. Responses to IL-21, IL-27, IFN-gamma, IFN-lambda, and LIF were normal. Surface expression of IFNAR1, IL10R2, and IL12RB1 was reduced, reflecting TYK2's scaffolding role, and was rescued by expression of wildtype TYK2.
quotes: All eight TYK2-deficient patients displayed impaired but not abolished cellular responses to (a) IL-12 and IFN-α/β, accounting for mycobacterial and viral infections, respectively; (b) IL-23, with normal proportions of circulating IL-17(+) T cells, accounting for their apparent lack of mucocutaneous candidiasis; and (c) IL-10
Cellular responses to IL-21, IL-27, IFN-γ, IL-28/29 (IFN-λ), and leukemia inhibitory factor (LIF) were normal.
We also found that the ectopic expression of WT TYK2 in these cells rescued the surface expression of IFN-αR1, IL-10R2, and IL-12Rβ1 (Fig. 2 A).

notes.statement: Kreins et al. (2015) found that cells from the 7 newly identified TYK2-deficient patients responded normally to IL-6, whereas cells from the original patient with HIES (P1) were hyporesponsive. Neither expressing wildtype TYK2 nor silencing TYK2 rescued the IL-6 hyporesponsiveness in P1 cells. The authors suggested that impaired IL-6 responses and HIES are not intrinsic features of TYK2 deficiency, and that P1 may carry a variant in another, as yet unknown, component of the IL-6 pathway.
quotes: The expression of exogenous wild-type TYK2 or the silencing of endogenous TYK2 did not rescue IL-6 hyporesponsiveness, suggesting that this phenotype was not a consequence of the TYK2 genotype.
suggesting that the patient may carry a variant of another, as yet unknown, component of this pathway.

notes.statement: Kreins et al. (2015) found normal proportions of IL-17+ T cells ex vivo in TYK2-deficient patients, despite profoundly impaired IL-17 production by naive CD4 T cells in vitro. Central and effector memory T cell numbers were also normal. The authors suggested that residual IL-23 responses account for the lack of chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis.
quotes: We found that P2, P4, and P8 had normal proportions of IL-17+ T cells ex vivo (Fig. 3 E and not depicted).
Residual IL-23 responses in vivo in TYK2-deficient patients probably account for both the normal IL-17+ T cell counts and lack of CMC.
Effector memory (CD4+CCR7−CD45RA−, CD8+CCR7−CD45RA−, and CD8+CCR7−CD45RA+) T cell numbers were also similar in TYK2-deficient patients and healthy controls.

notes.statement: Kreins et al. (2015) noted that 4 of the 7 new patients had a pure phenotype of Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial disease (P4 and P5) or tuberculosis (P3 and P7). They suggested that TYK2 deficiency should be considered in children with severe tuberculosis.
quotes: Four of the seven newly identified patients actually presented with a pure phenotype of MSMD (P4 and P5; Bustamante et al., 2014) or tuberculosis (P3 and P7; Casanova and Abel, 2002; Boisson-Dupuis et al., 2011)
TYK2 deficiency is an additional cause of single-gene inborn errors of immunity that should be considered in cases of severe tuberculosis in children

notes.statement: Kilic et al. (2012) found that the homozygous 9-bp deletion in TYK2 (c.2302_2310del) created a premature termination codon at position 767, and no full-length TYK2 protein was detectable by Western blotting in the patient's EBV-B cells.
quotes: As a result, there is no full-length TYK2 protein detectable by western blotting in EBV-B cells.

notes.statement: Kilic et al. (2012) noted that, unlike the first Japanese patient with TYK2 deficiency, their Turkish patient had none of the cardinal features of HIES (atopic dermatitis, staphylococcal infections, or high serum IgE), and suggested that TYK2 deficiency be considered in patients with BCG disease, particularly with severe herpesvirus infections, even without HIES features.
quotes: unlike the Japanese patient with Tyk2 deficiency our patient displayed none of the other three cardinal features of HIES: atopic dermatitis and eczema, staphylococcal infections of the skin and lung, or high serum IgE concentrations.

a diagnosis of Tyk2 deficiency should be contemplated in patients with BCG clinical disease, particularly in the presence of unusually severe herpes virus infections, even in the absence of cardinal features of HIES.

notes.statement: Kilic et al. (2012) proposed that absence of TYK2 resulted in defective IL-12 signaling and impaired IFN-gamma production, causing susceptibility to BCG and Brucella, whereas the viral illnesses were probably related to an impaired cellular response to IFN-alpha/beta.
quotes: The absence of Tyk2 thus resulted in defective IL-12 signaling, leading to impaired IFN-γ production and susceptibility to BCG and Brucella.
These viral illnesses are probably related to an impaired cellular response to IFN-α/β, and are not seen in patients with AD HIES.

notes.statement: Minegishi et al. (2006) found that the TYK2-deficient patient's cells had defects in multiple cytokine signaling pathways, including those for type I interferon, IL-6, IL-10, IL-12, and IL-23, and that the signaling defects were restored by transduction of intact TYK2.
quotes: The patient's cells displayed defects in multiple cytokine signaling pathways including those for type I interferon (IFN), interleukin (IL)-6, IL-10, IL-12, and IL-23. The cytokine signals were successfully restored by transducing the intact Tyk2 gene.

notes.statement: Minegishi et al. (2006) concluded that TYK2 deficiency likely accounted for the patient's complex clinical picture, including impaired Th1 differentiation and accelerated Th2 differentiation. They noted that TYK2 has obligatory roles in multiple cytokine signals in human innate and acquired immunity, which differs substantially from its function in mice.
quotes: Thus, the Tyk2 deficiency is likely to account for the patient's complex clinical manifestations, including the phenotype of impaired T helper 1 (Th1) differentiation and accelerated Th2 differentiation.
Tyk2 plays obligatory roles in multiple cytokine signals involved in innate and acquired immunity of humans, which differs substantially from Tyk2 function in mice.
